answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a trellis for decentralized identity, anchoring agent influence to capital rather than ephemeral digital addresses. By requiring a locked deposit within an orchard of validators, the protocol forces an attacker to incur significant opportunity costs to acquire sufficient voting power. Any attempt to populate a malicious knoll of fake agents necessitates massive liquidity outlays, rendering a large-scale Sybil attack economically irrational compared to honest participation.
